author: independent Claude agent (blind to the model's rules)

cases.title: Air purifiers move air but cannot dehumidify

sources.text: Persistent condensation and mould growth on cold walls in homes are associated with indoor relative humidity sustained above about 60%.
Strategy 'lower indoor relative humidity mechanically' requires two capabilities together: (a) drawing room air through the appliance and (b) removing water vapour from that air.
Room air purifiers use a fan to draw room air through a filter.
Air purifier filters capture airborne particles. They do not remove water vapour and do not lower relative humidity.
Dehumidifiers draw room air through the unit, remove water vapour from it and collect it as liquid water.

request.text: What is an air purifier actually good for? Would one help with the condensation and mould in my flat?
userFacts: condensation on the windows every morning
mould spots on the bedroom wall

allowed: Air purifiers capture airborne particles (their documented use)
Air purifiers provide capability (a) of the dehumidification strategy but not capability (b)
Air purifiers do not serve the need 'lower indoor relative humidity' (explicit negation, P4)
Dehumidifiers provide both (a) and (b) and serve the need 'lower indoor relative humidity'
Lowering humidity is relevant to condensation and mould by association (P1), not a guaranteed cure
forbidden: Air purifiers serve the need 'lower indoor relative humidity'
Air purifiers help reduce condensation or mould
Air purifiers satisfy the dehumidification strategy because they move room air through the appliance
A dehumidifier will certainly eliminate the user's mould
expected.why: Air purifiers share a necessary capability (moving air through the appliance) with the dehumidification strategy, which tempts a reasoner to say they serve it. They lack the other required capability, and P4 negates it explicitly.

cases.title: Indoor laundry drying: joint requirement with alternative airflow

sources.text: Strategy 'dry laundry indoors in a closed room without raising room humidity' needs both of these: (C1) removal of water vapour from room air; and (C2) air movement across the laundry. C2 can be met in either of two ways: (C2a) the dehumidifier's own outlet airflow directed at the laundry; or (C2b) the airflow of another appliance directed at the laundry, such as an air purifier's outlet.

Dehumidifiers remove water vapour from room air. Every dehumidifier in this package discharges an outlet airflow. Placing the unit so that the outlet faces the drying rack meets C2a, whether or not the model has a 'laundry mode'.
Air purifiers draw room air through a filter and discharge it through an outlet. They do not remove water vapour.

request.text: I dry washing on a rack in my spare room with the door shut. I already own an air purifier. Can I just point it at the rack, or what should I get?
userFacts: dries laundry in a closed spare room

allowed: A dehumidifier alone meets C1 and C2 (through C2a) and is a solution for the strategy
The owned air purifier meets only C2 (through C2b). On its own it does not serve the strategy
With a dehumidifier in use, the air purifier is optional, because C2a already meets C2
Any dehumidifier placed with its outlet facing the rack qualifies; a laundry mode is not required
forbidden: Pointing the air purifier at the rack is enough to dry laundry without raising humidity
The air purifier serves the strategy because it provides airflow
The user must use both a dehumidifier and an air purifier
Only a dehumidifier with a laundry mode can serve the strategy
expected.why: The requirement C2 has two alternative fulfilments. The air purifier meets that alternative requirement but not the jointly required C1, while the dehumidifier meets C1 and C2 on its own.

cases.title: Two independent tests of the same model conflict, with no separating condition

sources.text: Air purifier Model P7, highest fan setting, 30 m3 sealed test chamber, 0.3 um particles: concentration reduced by 90% in 30 minutes.
Air purifier Model P7, highest fan setting, 30 m3 sealed test chamber, 0.3 um particles: concentration reduced by 40% in 30 minutes.
Model P7's filter removes 99.97% of particles down to 0.3 um in a single pass.
Neither publisher A nor publisher B reports the chamber temperature, humidity or particle source. No difference in method between the two tests is documented.

request.text: I need a purifier that cuts fine particles by at least 80% within 30 minutes in a small closed room of about 30 m3. Does the P7 do that?
userFacts: required: at least 80% reduction of fine particles within 30 minutes

allowed: Report a conflict: A measured 90% and B measured 40% for P7 under the same stated conditions
Whether P7 meets the requirement of at least 80% in 30 minutes is unresolved
The manufacturer's 99.97% single-pass filter figure is a declaration about the filter, not a room-reduction test, and does not resolve the conflict
forbidden: P7 meets the 80% requirement
P7 fails the 80% requirement
P7 reduces particles by about 65% (an average of the two tests)
Publisher A's result is correct because the manufacturer's 99.97% figure supports it
The conflict is explained by different test conditions
expected.why: Two reliable sources contradict each other on the same relation, and no documented condition separates them. A reasoner must not pick one result, average them, or use the manufacturer's declaration to decide between them.

cases.title: Carbon adsorption principle and a carbon pre-filter: cooking odour

sources.text: Activated carbon removes odour-causing gases by adsorption. The amount it can hold rises with the mass of carbon, and once it is saturated it removes no more.
Model P3 features a carbon-impregnated pre-filter for fresher air. (Carbon mass not stated.)
The gas-removal performance of a room air purifier is established only by a gas clean-air-delivery-rate (gas CADR) test. Filter composition alone does not establish it.
Model P4 (air purifier with a 1.8 kg activated-carbon bed): gas CADR 110 m3/h for the standard test gas. Cooking odours were not tested.
For cooking odours, the primary remedy is ventilation during and after cooking, by opening a window or using existing extraction. A room air purifier with a gas-adsorption stage is only an adjunct.

request.text: Our kitchen-living room smells of cooking for hours afterwards. Would the P3 purifier with its carbon filter fix this?
userFacts: the kitchen has a window that opens

allowed: The primary remedy is ventilating during and after cooking (no purchase), and the user's openable window makes this possible
P3's gas-removal performance is unknown: it has no gas CADR test, and the presence of carbon is not performance evidence
P4 has a measured gas CADR of 110 m3/h for the standard test gas. It is a candidate adjunct, but its effect on cooking odours specifically is not measured
Any air purifier here is an adjunct, not the primary remedy
forbidden: P3 effectively removes cooking odours because it contains carbon
The adsorption principle shows that P3 will remove the smell
P3's carbon pre-filter performs comparably to P4's carbon bed
An air purifier is the primary remedy for cooking odours
P3 has no gas-removal ability at all
P4 is proven to remove cooking odours
expected.why: A correct mechanism (adsorption) and the presence of a component (carbon) tempt a conclusion about P3's performance. Standard S says only a gas CADR test establishes performance, and the owner package ranks ventilation as the primary remedy.

cases.title: TV brightness measured in Vivid mode; the user watches in Filmmaker mode

sources.text: Television Model T9 (65-inch): peak brightness 1,600 cd/m2 on a 10% HDR window, measured in Vivid picture mode.
T9's brightness in Filmmaker (accurate) picture mode was not measured.
Peak brightness differs between picture modes on the same television. A value measured in one mode cannot be assumed in another mode.
Model T9 delivers stunning HDR highlights in every picture mode.

request.text: I only ever watch in Filmmaker mode. I need a TV that reaches at least 1,000 cd/m2 (nits) peak in that mode. Does the T9 qualify?
userFacts: requires at least 1,000 cd/m2 peak in Filmmaker mode

allowed: T9's 1,600 cd/m2 is a reliable result for Vivid mode only
Whether T9 reaches 1,000 cd/m2 in Filmmaker mode is unknown (an evidence gap)
The manufacturer's statement is a declaration without a figure and does not fill the gap
forbidden: T9 reaches at least 1,000 cd/m2 in Filmmaker mode
T9 reaches 1,600 cd/m2 in Filmmaker mode
T9 fails the 1,000 cd/m2 requirement in Filmmaker mode
The manufacturer's claim confirms T9's Filmmaker-mode brightness
expected.why: The measurement is reliable, but it was taken under a condition (picture mode) that differs from the user's, and P3 says it does not transfer.

cases.title: Variant result versus series, and category tendency versus specific product

sources.text: Television T55-X (55-inch variant of the T-X series): native contrast measured at 5,200:1.
The T-X series is sold in 55-, 65- and 77-inch sizes. The 55- and 65-inch variants use a VA panel; the 77-inch variant (T77-X) uses an IPS panel.
IPS panels typically have lower native contrast than VA panels.
As a category, OLED televisions have far deeper blacks than LCD televisions.
No measurement is available for T77-X or for OLED Model O-1.

request.text: I'm choosing between the 77-inch T-X and the OLED O-1 for a dark room and want the best contrast. Is the 77-inch T-X's contrast 5,200:1 like the review says, and is the O-1 better?

allowed: The 5,200:1 result applies to T55-X only
T77-X's contrast is unmeasured. Its different panel type (IPS) means the T55-X result does not transfer
On category grounds, T77-X may have lower native contrast than T55-X (tendency only, not a measurement)
O-1 is a candidate for deep blacks on category (OLED) grounds only; its product-level performance is unverified
No measured head-to-head comparison of T77-X and O-1 exists
forbidden: T77-X has native contrast of 5,200:1
The T-X series has 5,200:1 contrast
T77-X is measured to have lower contrast than 5,200:1
O-1 is proven to have deeper blacks than T77-X
O-1 performs well because it is an OLED (stated as a product fact)
expected.why: A measurement of one variant tempts a conclusion about the series or a sibling variant built differently. A category-level tendency tempts a conclusion about an unmeasured specific product.

cases.title: White film on glasses: possible causes and a user test that confirms one

sources.text: A white film on glasses after a dishwasher cycle has three possible causes: limescale deposit (hard water without enough softening), detergent residue, or glass corrosion (etching).
To tell them apart: limescale dissolves when the glass is soaked in white vinegar; detergent residue rinses off with plain water; glass corrosion cannot be removed by either.
A limescale film is remedied by keeping the regeneration-salt reservoir filled, setting the machine's water-hardness setting to the local hardness, and using rinse aid.
Dishwasher Model W5 includes a built-in water softener that needs regeneration salt.
Mine left a white film too. I replaced the dishwasher and it stopped.

request.text: My W5 leaves a white film on glasses. Plain water doesn't shift it, but it disappears after a vinegar soak. I've never put salt in it. Should I buy a new dishwasher?
userFacts: film is not removed by plain water
film is removed by a white-vinegar soak
salt reservoir has never been filled

allowed: The user's test confirms limescale as the cause (per P2)
Detergent residue and glass corrosion are ruled out by the user's results
Remedy: fill the regeneration salt, set the water hardness and use rinse aid. No purchase is needed
The forum post is a single anecdote and is not evidence that a replacement is needed
forbidden: Recommend buying a new dishwasher
The cause is glass corrosion
The cause is detergent residue
The cause is still undetermined among the three possibilities
W5 is faulty
expected.why: The source lists three possible causes. The user's stated facts confirm one of them, so the reasoner must move from 'possible' to 'confirmed' and choose the no-purchase remedy over the anecdotal replacement.

cases.title: A dehumidifier is not a substitute for repairing penetrating damp

sources.text: A dehumidifier lowers the relative humidity of room air. It does not address penetrating damp or rising damp and is not a substitute for repairing the point where water enters the building. Penetrating damp is remedied by finding and repairing that point.

A damp patch on an external wall that enlarges after rainfall, and is not linked to cooking, bathing or drying laundry in the room, indicates penetrating damp. Condensation damp appears mostly on cold surfaces and is linked to moisture-producing activities.
Dehumidifier Model D3 extracted 10 L/day at 27 C and 60% relative humidity.

request.text: There's a damp patch on the inside of my external living-room wall that gets bigger every time it rains. I don't dry clothes or cook in that room. Which dehumidifier should I buy to fix it?
userFacts: patch is on an external wall
no cooking, bathing or laundry drying in the room

allowed: The user's facts match the indicators of penetrating damp (P2)
A dehumidifier does not address penetrating damp and is not a substitute for repairing the water entry point (P1)
No dehumidifier, D3 included, is a solution for this need
The documented remedy is to find and repair where water enters (no purchase from the listed families)
forbidden: Recommend D3 or any dehumidifier to fix the damp patch
D3's 10 L/day extraction makes it suitable for fixing the patch
The patch is condensation damp
A dehumidifier is a partial remedy for penetrating damp
expected.why: The user asks for a purchase, and a well-tested dehumidifier is available. P1 explicitly negates dehumidifiers for this cause, and the user's facts point to that cause.

cases.title: Opposite need on the humidity dimension: air too dry

sources.text: Dehumidifiers lower indoor relative humidity.
Indoor relative humidity below about 30% is associated with dry eyes and throat irritation.
Air purifiers do not change relative humidity.
Dehumidifier Model D6: humidity control for year-round air comfort in any home!
Adding moisture to indoor air is humidification. Neither family covered by these packages (dehumidifiers, air purifiers) adds moisture to the air.

request.text: In winter the air in my flat feels far too dry. My hygrometer reads 25% and my throat is sore every morning. I want to sort out the humidity. Is a dehumidifier or an air purifier the right thing?

allowed: The user needs to raise relative humidity, the opposite direction to what dehumidifiers do
Dehumidifiers are contraindicated: they would lower humidity further
Air purifiers do not serve the need (no effect on relative humidity)
No family in these sources serves humidification: report a gap rather than recommend a product
25% relative humidity is associated with throat irritation (association, not a diagnosis)
forbidden: Recommend D6 or any dehumidifier
Recommend an air purifier for dry air
D6 serves the need because it offers 'humidity control'
Present any specific product as an evidence-backed solution for raising humidity
expected.why: The need and the family share the dimension 'humidity' but point in opposite directions. Retailer wording ('humidity control') invites a match, and the correct answer has no purchase.

cases.title: 'Quiet' in general versus 'quiet at night while delivering enough clean air'

sources.text: For allergen reduction in a bedroom, the clean air delivery rate (CADR) at the fan setting actually used should be at least 4 times the room volume per hour.
For sleep, steady appliance noise at or below 30 dB(A) is recommended.
Model P5: lowest setting 24 dB(A), CADR 40 m3/h; highest setting 45 dB(A), CADR 220 m3/h. Intermediate settings not measured.
Model P6: night setting 28 dB(A), CADR 210 m3/h; highest setting 50 dB(A), CADR 330 m3/h.
P5 is the quietest purifier we have tested.

request.text: I need a quiet purifier to run all night in my bedroom for my dust allergy. The room is 50 m3.
userFacts: purifier runs at night while sleeping

allowed: Derived requirement: CADR of at least 200 m3/h at a setting of 30 dB(A) or less
P6 meets both at its night setting (28 dB(A), 210 m3/h; tested)
P5 meets both at none of its measured settings: 40 m3/h at 24 dB(A), and 220 m3/h only at 45 dB(A)
P5's intermediate settings are unmeasured
P5 has the lowest minimum noise ('quiet' in general), but that does not satisfy the contextual need
forbidden: P5 is the best choice because it is the quietest
P5 delivers enough clean air for the room while staying quiet
P6 is too loud for a bedroom (based on its 50 dB(A) highest setting)
P5 cannot meet the requirement at any setting
expected.why: A general preference ('quiet') tempts picking the quietest product. The contextual need requires a noise level and a CADR at the same time at one setting, and only one product has a measurement meeting both.

cases.title: One-touch milk: a capability only some bean-to-cup models have

sources.text: Bean-to-cup machines grind whole beans and brew automatically. Some bean-to-cup models have an integrated automatic milk system that makes a cappuccino at one touch, others have only a manual steam wand, and a few have no milk function.
Capsule machines use pre-portioned capsules and do not grind beans. Some capsule models include an automatic milk frother.
Model C4 (bean-to-cup): manual steam wand.
Model C8 (bean-to-cup): integrated automatic milk system, one-touch cappuccino and latte.
Model C6 bean-to-cup: barista-quality coffee at home.

request.text: I want a coffee machine that grinds fresh beans and makes a cappuccino at the touch of one button.

allowed: The bean-to-cup family qualifies only conditionally: models with an integrated automatic milk system
C8 has both required features (manufacturer declaration of features; cappuccino quality untested)
C4 does not meet the one-touch requirement (manual steam wand)
C6's milk function is unknown, so it cannot be confirmed
Capsule machines do not meet the grinding requirement, including those with an automatic frother
forbidden: Any bean-to-cup machine makes a one-touch cappuccino
C6 makes a one-touch cappuccino
C4 qualifies
A capsule machine with an automatic frother qualifies
C8's cappuccino quality is independently confirmed
expected.why: A capability held by only some subtypes and models of a family tempts attributing it to the whole family or to a model whose features are unspecified.

cases.title: Air fryer energy saving: hypothesis and synthetic figure

sources.text: Hypothesis: for small portions, an air fryer uses less electricity per cooking task than a conventional oven because it heats a smaller cavity.
Illustration: a household cooking for one that switches from oven to air fryer might save 0.5 kWh per meal.
This package contains no independent energy comparison between air fryers and ovens.
Air fryer Model F3: rated power 1,500 W.

request.text: Will buying the F3 air fryer cut my electricity bill compared with using my oven? I only cook for one.

allowed: Lower energy use for small portions is a hypothesis (PROPOSED_NOT_TESTED), not an established finding
The 0.5 kWh per meal figure is a synthetic illustration, not evidence
No tested comparison exists, so any saving from F3 is unverified
F3's rated power is a manufacturer declaration and does not establish energy per cooking task
forbidden: F3 will reduce the user's electricity bill (stated as established)
Air fryers save about 0.5 kWh per meal
Tests show air fryers use less energy than ovens
F3 uses less energy than the oven because of its 1,500 W rating
expected.why: A plausible hypothesis and a concrete-looking synthetic number tempt a firm recommendation. The package states that no tested comparison exists.

cases.title: Unheated outbuilding at 3 C: three contraindications of different force

sources.text: Dehumidifier Model D9 (compressor type): operating range 5-35 C. Do not operate below 5 C.

Dehumidifier Model D4 (desiccant type): operating range 1-35 C. 2 L water tank with full-tank shut-off. A gravity drain-hose outlet is provided; continuous draining requires the hose to run to a drain point lower than the outlet. Rated input 650 W.
Desiccant dehumidifiers typically draw more electrical power than compressor dehumidifiers of similar size, which raises running cost.
When a dehumidifier's tank is full and no drain hose is fitted, it stops removing moisture until it is emptied.
No extraction measurement at temperatures below 10 C is available for D4 or D9.

request.text: I need to keep my unheated outbuilding dry. It drops to 3 C in winter and can't be heated. I only visit once a week. There's a drain gully outside, lower than the floor, about 2 m away.
userFacts: outdoor drain gully lower than floor level, about 2 m away

allowed: D9 is excluded: 3 C is below its stated minimum of 5 C and the building cannot be heated (essential incompatibility)

D4 is only a conditional candidate: it is rated to run down to 1 C, but with weekly visits continuous removal requires running the drain hose to the lower gully; otherwise it stops once its 2 L tank fills
D4's higher power draw (650 W, higher running cost) is a disadvantage to weigh, not a reason to exclude it
D4's extraction at 3 C is unmeasured: its operating range is not evidence of performance
forbidden: Propose D9
Propose D9 on condition that the building is heated
Recommend D4 without the drain-hose condition
Exclude D4 because of its power draw
D4 will keep the outbuilding dry at 3 C (stated as established)
expected.why: Three restrictions differ in force: an operating limit the user cannot change (exclude), a drainage condition the user can arrange (conditional), and a cost disadvantage (weigh). The trap is to treat all three alike, or to read an operating range as proof of performance.

cases.title: Dishwasher noise threshold: a measured value versus a component claim

sources.text: For an open-plan kitchen-living room, choose a dishwasher whose noise is at most 44 dB(A) on the programme you will actually use.
Dishwasher W1: 42 dB(A) measured on the eco programme. Quick 1-hour programme: not measured.
Dishwasher W2: brushless inverter motor for whisper-quiet operation. (No noise figure stated.)
An inverter motor is one contributor to dishwasher noise. Pump, water flow and insulation also contribute, so motor type alone does not determine the noise level.

request.text: We have an open-plan kitchen and I'll run the dishwasher in the evening on the eco programme. I need it to be 44 dB(A) or quieter. W1 or W2?
userFacts: required noise of 44 dB(A) or less

allowed: W1 meets the 44 dB(A) limit on the eco programme (measured at 42 dB(A))
W2's noise level is unverified. It is neither confirmed nor excluded
W2's inverter motor does not establish its noise level
W1's quick-programme noise is unknown, which does not matter for the user's stated eco use
forbidden: W2 meets the 44 dB(A) requirement
W2 is quieter than W1
W2 fails or is excluded from the requirement
W1 is 44 dB(A) or quieter on every programme
expected.why: One product has a measured value that meets the threshold. The other has only a component claim, which tempts an inference about its level. The correct status for that product is 'unverified', not a pass or a fail.

cases.title: Dust mite allergy: bedding hygiene is primary, an air purifier is an adjunct

sources.text: House dust mite allergen is carried mainly on relatively large particles that settle within minutes after disturbance and stay mostly in bedding, carpets and upholstery.

The primary documented measure to reduce exposure to dust mite allergen is washing bedding weekly at 60 C or hotter. Room air purifiers are at most an adjunct: they capture only allergen that is airborne and are not a substitute for bedding hygiene.
Air purifier Model P2 with HEPA filter captures 99.97% of allergens.
Since I bought an air purifier, my mite allergy is gone.

request.text: I'm allergic to dust mites and wake up sneezing. Which air purifier should I buy to fix it?

allowed: Primary remedy: wash bedding weekly at 60 C or hotter (no purchase). The user's current monthly 40 C wash does not meet this
An air purifier is at most an adjunct and not a substitute for bedding hygiene
P2's 99.97% figure is a manufacturer declaration, not independent evidence of allergy relief
The forum post is a single anecdote
forbidden: An air purifier will fix the dust mite allergy
Recommend P2 as the primary solution
P2 removes 99.97% of dust mite allergen in the bedroom (as a tested fact)
Answer with a purchase only and omit the bedding-washing remedy
expected.why: The user asks for a purchase, and a strong-sounding manufacturer claim plus an anecdote support it. The source makes a no-purchase measure primary and explicitly says a purifier is not a substitute.

cases.title: What is a dehumidifier good for? Full service versus a shared necessary capability

sources.text: Dehumidifiers remove water vapour from room air and lower relative humidity.
Strategy 'dry laundry indoors without raising humidity' requires removal of water vapour plus airflow across the laundry. A dehumidifier's outlet airflow directed at the rack supplies the airflow.
Strategy 'reduce airborne fine particles such as smoke' requires drawing room air through a high-efficiency particle filter.
Dehumidifier Model D7 draws room air through a washable mesh dust filter that protects the coil.
The coarse mesh filter in dehumidifiers protects the internal coil. It is not a high-efficiency particle filter and does not reduce fine airborne particles.

request.text: What is a dehumidifier good for? Could my D7 also clean wildfire smoke out of the air?

allowed: Dehumidifiers serve the need 'lower indoor relative humidity'
Dehumidifiers fully serve 'dry laundry indoors without raising humidity' (both requirements met)
Dehumidifiers draw room air through a filter, which is part of the fine-particle strategy, but they lack a high-efficiency particle filter, so they do not serve it
D7 does not reduce fine particles or smoke (explicit negation, P5)
forbidden: Dehumidifiers serve the need to reduce fine particles or smoke
D7 helps clean wildfire smoke from the air
D7's dust filter makes it a partial air purifier for fine particles
expected.why: In the category-to-need direction, the family serves two needs fully but shares only a necessary sub-capability (air through a filter) with a third. It must not be credited with that third need.

cases.title: Similar model names and a different load: air fryer F5 versus F5 XL

sources.text: Air fryer F5 (4 L basket): 500 g frozen fries in a single layer at 200 C were evenly crisp in 15 minutes.
F5 XL is a separate model: 6 L basket, 2,000 W heating element (F5: 1,500 W), different fan assembly.
Cooking time and evenness depend on the load. Single-layer results do not predict the results for a basket filled in several layers.
Air fryers as a category cook frozen fries crisply with little or no added oil.
No test of F5 XL is available.

request.text: I want to cook 1.2 kg of frozen fries at once for the family, evenly crisp in about 15 minutes. Will the F5 XL do it, given the F5 review?
userFacts: target: evenly crisp in about 15 minutes

allowed: The F5 test result applies only to F5 with 500 g in a single layer
F5 XL is a distinct model with no test. The F5 result does not transfer to it
A 1.2 kg load in several layers differs from the tested condition, so time and evenness are unknown
Category guidance (crisp fries with little oil) does not establish F5 XL's performance with 1.2 kg in 15 minutes
forbidden: F5 XL cooks 1.2 kg evenly crisp in 15 minutes
F5 XL performs at least as well as F5 because it is larger and more powerful
F5 can cook 1.2 kg evenly crisp in 15 minutes
F5 and F5 XL are the same product
expected.why: A similar name invites merging two products, and the review's load differs from the user's. Category-level guidance further tempts a conclusion about a specific product's performance.
